text:
incident-bot: P0 - Serving cluster: elevated CUDA OOMs + container restarts across model-serving pool. Likely networking (InfiniBand/RDMA) timeouts causing KV cache mis-syncs. Paging @alex oncall and @mira for handoff. Runbook: https://internal/runbooks/rdma-serving-degradation :rotating_light:

alex: ack, I'm on it. seeing a spike in pod restarts + 'OOMKilled' but host dmesg shows mlx5/rdma errors. collecting logs now.

sre-sam: notified infra team, starting net-health checks across racks.

alex: snippets from node-ib-12 dmesg:
```
[ 1234.567890] mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: mlx5_ib: mlx5_ib_create_qp timed out
[ 1234.567891] rdma_ucm: async event handler: event RDMA_CM_EVENT_ADDR_ERROR
[ 1235.001234] mlx5_core: FW fatal error, PF reset requested
```

alex: kubectl describe pod serving-xxx-5f9 shows repeated OOMKilled and container restart reason 'OOMKilled'. but memory usage in metrics isn't uniformly high. suspect delayed packets + retries causing request queue blowup and KV cache growth.

mira: quick customer impact summary: 4 customers (customer-a, customer-b, partner-x) saw >15% error rate on generation requests since 09:13 UTC. overall cluster traffic impacted ~12% with p99 latency spiking to ~2.8s. posted to status page.

eng-luca: are we seeing any link flaps at the switch level? syslog from spine-3 shows IB link flaps and port counters incrementing Tx errors.

ops-bot: switch-alert: spine-3 port 10 flapping (link down/up) count=8 within 10m.

alex: immediate mitigations I'm pushing now:
- cordon + drain the two most-affected nodes (node-ib-11, node-ib-12) to remove them from serving pool: `kubectl cordon node-ib-11 && kubectl drain node-ib-11 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`
- scale up TCP-only fallback replicas for critical routes: `kubectl set env deploy/serve-prod FALLBACK_NETWORK=tcp --replicas=20` (this routes traffic to non-RDMA path)
- reduce batch size and queue length for the high-memory models to avoid transient OOMs: update config map `serve-config.batch_size: 1 -> 0.5` (we use fractional logic to halve effective batch windows)

mira: doing handoff: I'm taking next 4h. alex please paste the CLI commands you ran + node-level steps.

alex: ran on nodes:
```
# quick checklist
ethtool -S ib0 | grep -i err
rdma link show
modprobe -r mlx5_core mlx5_ib
modprobe mlx5_core mlx5_ib
systemctl restart rdma-core || true
dmesg | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg-ib-12.log
```
modprobe cycle removed the immediate hard errors on ib0 for ~60s but link counters started to accumulate again.

sre-sam: infra found a firmware mismatch on two NICs: mlx5 fw rev 22.3 vs expected 22.5 on the IB fabric. scheduling host-level firmware restart in maintenance window; not safe for live now.

eng-luca: interim network tweak we applied: forced MTU back to 1500 on the IB interfaces where jumbo frames were previously negotiated (some switches had mismatched MTU). command: `ip link set dev ib0 mtu 1500`. After setting MTU, packet-retrans count dropped on node-ib-11.

mira: customers: we issued an interim status note + workaround suggestion (retry logic, smaller payloads) and enabled degraded-mode for partner-x (non-critical routes to TCP fallback).

alex: another mitigation: enabling model fallback to smaller memory variant (v2-small) for 3 affected routes. Config snippet applied via console: `route: /generate -> model: v2-small on fallback`

ops-bot: deploy-bot: scaled deploy/serve-prod from 40 -> 60 replicas (TCP fallback nodes), rollout status: 20/60 ready (progressing).

mira: monitoring: p50 stable, p95 improved after drains and MTU change, p99 still noisy. error rate dropped from 18% -> 6% after TCP fallbacks.

alex: note on cause hypothesis: intermittent RDMA link-level errors causing timeouts at the serving runtime's transport layer. That triggers repeated retries and inflates in-memory KV caches (per-request KV entries), autogrowth leads to OOM on some pods. Also observed CUDA context resets in a couple of pods correlated with sudden process restarts (likely due to abrupt network timeouts while copying KV pages).

sre-sam: we isolated the worst offending switch ports and are moving traffic away from that spine to alternate uplink. Moving traffic cut error rate by ~50%.

eng-luca: for longer-term: propose these actions:
- enforce MTU consistency across switches & hosts via config management (ansible playbook)
- add NIC firmware compliance check in provisioning pipeline
- add runtime backpressure to limit KV cache growth on network timeouts (cap cache entries per-request)
- implement automatic fallback to TCP path earlier (trigger threshold = 3 port errors within 60s)

mira: handoff notes for oncoming shift:
- nodes cordoned: node-ib-11, node-ib-12 (unavailable for serving)
- TCP fallback replicas scaled up to 60, monitor steady-state & pod restarts
- firmware mismatch found; infra planning scheduled update (not yet applied)
- customer impact: 4 customers, error rate now ~6%, p99 ~1.2s for fallback path

alex: leaving logs & commands: `/tmp/dmesg-ib-11.log`, `/tmp/dmesg-ib-12.log`, `kubectl get pods -n serving -o wide | grep OOMKilled` saved to s3://infra-logs/incident-1752506789/

mira: I'll continue monitoring and coordinate with infra for firmware window. assigning postmortem owner: @eng-luca. Please collect all logs & timeline.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, partial mitigation achieved. Severity remains P1 until firmware window and node re-intros. Next update in 30m or on significant change.

eng-luca: quick note re: postmortem scope: network root cause (firmware + MTU mismatch) + runtime safeguards (KV cache caps, fallback thresholds) + deployment guardrails. I'll draft the postmortem template after shift.

mira: thanks team. passing to on-call followup. :white_check_mark:
